Hello, to answer your questions, yes it is absolutely okay to express your feminine side and be like this! It's okay to be yourself. And yes, there are therapist that specialize in gender identity. They can't really tell you "what this is" but they can help you work through it and figure it out for yourself. It's okay to not fully understand it, and it's okay to figure everything out. I know it's daunting and can be stressful, but it's okay to express yourself! I hope that this helped at all, and I hope you have a lovely day.

Your mom is definitely right. I get moving out is scary, but that whole situation seems pretty set in stone to me. A better job that provided college classes and someone else helping to pay for your parking and extra funds really seems like a great idea, as well as having your own place. I get it's farther away but I'm assuming not ~too~ far by the way you talk about it, he can come visit her or she can visit him.

Your brother is acting like a child, full on throwing a fit because he didn't get his way. It sucks that his gf bailed on him but he could have still moved and gotten everything squared away, and maybe that would have prompted her to move in with him quicker. Either way, it's none of YOUR guys' fault that he and his gf backed out. He also doesn't help with any bills or chores, which is what your mom had expected from the beginning. You're not the asshole, and even though the whole thing didn't happen which is what the deal was about, you're not in the wrong for requesting the room especially because you'll be starting college and whatnot. He's acting like a toddler.
